name: Field Doctor-Style Thai Green Chicken Curry (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
680 g Chicken
400 g Broccoli
285 g Whole grain rice
1 medium Aubergine
240 g Edamame (SOY bean)
185 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
185 g Green Beans
125 g Extra Virgin Olive Oil
80 g Coconut Milk [Coconut, Water]
80 g Peas
65 g Red Quinoa
2 1/2 tbsp Ginger
23 g Chives
2 tsp Fish Sauce (Anchovy (FISH) (Encrasicholina spp), Salt, Sugar], Turmeric Blend, Tapioca Starch, Galangal, Coriander, Brown Sugar, Basil, Lime Leaf, Red Chilli, Lemongrass, Sea Salt, Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Fennel Ground, Nutmeg Ground, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Grains: Cook wholegrain rice and red quinoa; drain and keep warm.

2. Aromatics: Warm olive oil with ginger, galangal, lemongrass, lime leaf and a little red chilli (to taste). Soften chives briefly.

3. Curry: Add diced chicken and brown lightly. Stir in broccoli, aubergine, green beans, edamame and peas. Pour in coconut milk, soy milk, fish sauce, brown sugar, turmeric blend, chicken stock and water as needed. Simmer until chicken is cooked and vegetables are tender.

4. Finish: Thicken lightly with tapioca slurry if you want a coating sauce. Stir through basil and coriander. Serve over the rice–quinoa.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Chicken, Water, Broccoli, Whole grain rice, Aubergine, Edamame (SOY bean), Soy Milk [SOY beans, water], Green Beans...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Thai Green Chicken Curry (Low FODMAP) (~381 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/green-curry
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~381 g x 8 = 3048 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~399 g (inferred ~13.10% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Extra Virgin Olive Oil is kept as an ingredient on this recipe because the ready meal is relatively oil-rich (or pesto-style); still fry/roast in extra virgin olive oil as directed.
